To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
polyploid tumors with a higher number of centrosome per cell were more resistant to endocrine therapy.

We found cells with three and more centrosomes and a higher average number centrosomes per nucleus in the polyploidy tumors than in the non-polyploid tumors, and in the endocrine therapy resistant tumors than in the responsive tumors.
Centrosome ampliﬁcation leads to aberrant cell division giving rise to aneuryploidy and it is associated with poor prognosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of centrosomes in polyploidy in mouse mammary tumors and the relationship with hormone responsiveness.
the role of polyploidy in the development of breast tumors and the relationship with the response to hormone treatment.
the role of centrosomes and centrosome abnormalities in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
centrosome amplifications and polyploidies are associated with resistance to endocrine treatment.
centrosome amplifications are associated with polyploidy in luminal mammary tumors and that this is a characteristic of the endocrine therapy resistant tumors.
polyploidy in luminal breast cancer is associated with endocrine therapy resistance, which may be mediated through centrosome amplifications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polyploidy is an early event in the progression of breast cancer and that it is a marker of poor response to endocrine therapy.
the centrosome ampliﬁcation in polyploidy tumors is associated with endocrine therapy resistance in luminal breast cancer.
the centrosome amplifications and polyploidy are associated with the resistance to the endocrine therapy in luminal breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
centrosome abnormalities and polyploidy are associated with the lack of response to endocrine therapy.

centrosome amplifications and polyploidy are more common in tumors that are resistant to endocrine treatment, and that the number of centrosome amplifying cells is greater in the endocrine resistant tumors.
centrosome abnormalities and polyploidy may play an important role in the resistance to hormone therapy in breast cancer.
